newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares slightly rise on late buying.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares slightly rise on late buying.

text.p: Istanbul shares rose 1.04 percent on average on reaction buys on Tueday afternoon after falling 0.39 percent in morning trade, brokers said.
The IMKB National-100 closed at 1,548, up 16 points from Monday's 1,532 and the trade volume eased to 17.07 trillion lira from 20.66 trillion.
Brokers said some buying emerged after the treasury sold 133 trillion lira worth of two-year inflation-indexed bonds at a lower cost, which raised confidence in the market.
Although the banks will pay the treasury 131.7 trillion lira for the bond auction on Wednesday, 199 trillion lira will be cashed in from t-bill maturities.

But the central bank will make a 42-day reverse repo auction on the open market operations on Wednesday to drain around 67 trillion lira excess cash. The bank also lent banks through money market operations with Wednesday's value.

"The market was expecting the last minute buys at these levels. The auction result also prompted buying. We may see an upward movement tomorrow depending on the last minute buying but trading will be in a limited range," said Tolga Ozkan Okay from Evis Securities.
The shares have been easing recently due to a cash shortage in the market, political uncertainties and reluctance to buy ahead of a 4-1/2 day holiday which starts on April 17.

The religious holiday between April 17-21 will be followed by an official holiday on April 23. The government has declared April 22 a holiday for state offices but it is not yet known if the markets will be closed.
Of the 240 shares traded, 101 shares were closed above Monday close, 76 were close below yesterday levels and 63 finished stable.
IMKB Industrial rose 0.65 percent to 1,537, IMKB Services was up 1.11 percent to 1,454, and IMKB Financial firmed 1.40 percent to 1,666.

Top actives were utility Cukurova Elektrik, up 2,500 lira at 220,000, car producer Otosan, up 2,000 at 75,000 and state oil refiner Tupras, up 2,000 AT 65,000. They made up 22 percent of total turnover.
